quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A one-way street is starting.
A one-way street is ending.
A divided highway is starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead becomes a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other factors?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05%. Being awake for 24 hours has the same effect as a blood alcohol level of 0.10%.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not move until all gates are up and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes driving conditions not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes driving conditions not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when conditions are not ideal. You can be ticketed for speeding even at the posted limit if conditions are poor.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area.
The highest or lowest speed allowed by law.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in poor conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed allowed by law.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed. The posted limits are for ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions require it.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: A flashing yellow light will appear soon.
A steady green light will appear soon.
A steady red light will appear soon.
A flashing red light will appear soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steady red light will appear soon.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: You see one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line down the center of the road. The broken line is next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
questions.explanation: When one line is solid and one is broken, you can pass from the side next to the broken line if it is safe.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge and slow down.
Move to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles using lights and sirens. Move to the right edge and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what lights should you use?

options.text: Turn off all lights.
Use parking lights only.
Use headlights only.
Turn on emergency flashers and low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and low beams.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the road at night, turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights. This makes sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers that pedestrians may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. To avoid road rage, just let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to a police officer?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. You must show your insurance card and license to a police officer after a traffic stop or collision if asked.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.
Do not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after you stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn when the arrow is red.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid on water, you should quickly apply the brakes.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids on water, try to regain control. If you cannot, let off the accelerator and ride out the skid. Do not apply the brakes right away.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: Pavement is very slippery when it first starts to rain.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Give yourself more space to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain starts. Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Slow down and increase your stopping distance on wet roads to keep your tires from losing grip.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in the blood may affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely. Any alcohol can hurt your judgment and physical coordination. Driving after drinking any amount of alcohol can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car ahead.
Drive carefully and do not slow down to look at things.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully and do not slow down to look at things.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual things. This causes traffic jams. Drive carefully through construction zones without looking around.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events on the road:

options.text: Creates traffic jams.
Stops rear-end crashes.
Improves traffic flow by preventing crashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Creates traffic jams.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down just to look at accidents or unusual events. This slowing causes traffic jams. Avoid this behavior to help traffic flow smoothly.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. Wait until the gate is raised. Then only cross the tracks if you can see clearly in both directions and you are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to share half a lane.
Pass the motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcyclists a full lane width. Even if space looks tight, motorcycles need room to move safely.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your focus away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your focus away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means doing anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving. It is the most common cause of traffic crashes. Any distraction makes drivers miss important sights and sounds needed to avoid a crash.
